<problem>
Call a set $A\subseteq\mathbb N_0$ *explicit* if there is a deterministic algorithm that decides whether $n\in A$ in time polynomial in $\log n$. For $A\subseteq\mathbb N_0$ let $\sigma_A(n)=|\{(a,a')\in A^2:\ a+a'=n\}|$ be the number of ordered representations of $n$ as a sum of two elements of $A$. Erdős proved by probabilistic methods that there is $A$ with $A+A=\mathbb N_0$ and $c_1\log n\le\sigma_A(n)\le c_2\log n$ for all $n\ge2$, while the best explicit construction known (Jain–Pham–Sawhney–Zakharov) only gives $\sigma_A(n)\le n^{c/\log\log n}$.

Question 1. Does there exist an explicit set $A\subseteq\mathbb N_0$ with $A+A=\mathbb N_0$ and a constant $C$ such that $\sigma_A(n)\le(\log n)^{C}$ for all $n\ge2$?

Question 2 (weaker). Does there exist an explicit $A$ with $A+A=\mathbb N_0$ and $\sigma_A(n)\le\exp\big((\log n)^{1-\delta}\big)$ for some constant $\delta>0$ and all large $n$?
</problem>

<solution>
STATUS: Neither Question 1 nor Question 2 is resolved here; to my knowledge both are open (JPSZ's n^{c/log log n} is the record). What I prove: (A) a folklore explicit construction with sigma_A(n) <= n^eps for any eps>0; (B) an exact equivalence of Q1/Q2 with a single-scale finite derandomization problem; plus an analysis of barriers.

0. Conventions. log = log_2. For finite S, r_S(m)=#{(s,s') in S^2: s+s'=m}, R(S)=max_m r_S(m). A family (S_ell), S_ell subset [0,2^ell), is "uniformly explicit" if one algorithm decides x in S_ell in time poly(ell) on input (ell,x). Bounds like sigma_A(n) <= (log n)^C are for n >= n_0 (equivalently <= C'(log(n+2))^C for all n).

1. Mixed-radix lemma. Let 1<=ell_1<ell_2<..., b_i=2^{ell_i}, B_1=1, B_{i+1}=B_i b_i; every n has a unique expansion n=sum n_i B_i, 0<=n_i<b_i; d(n)=largest i with n_i != 0. Given S_i subset [0,b_i) with S_i+S_i containing [0,b_i), let A={a: a_i in S_i for all i}. Then
(a) A+A = N_0: choose s_i+s_i'=n_i in S_i, set a=sum s_i B_i, a'=sum s_i' B_i (no carries).
(b) sigma_A(n) <= 2^{d-1} prod_{i<=d} R(S_i), d=d(n). Proof: if a+a'=n then a_i=a_i'=0 for i>d. Define c_1=0, c_{i+1}=floor((a_i+a_i'+c_i)/b_i) in {0,1}; then a_i+a_i'+c_i=n_i+b_i c_{i+1}, and telescoping gives c_{d+1}=0. So (a,a') is determined by the carry vector (c_2..c_d) in {0,1}^{d-1} and, for each i, a representation of n_i+b_i c_{i+1}-c_i in S_i+S_i (at most R(S_i) choices).
(c) If (S_ell) is uniformly explicit and ell_i>=i, A is explicit: d(n)<=log n, digits via d(n) divisions, each membership test poly(ell_i) <= poly(log n).

2. Theorem A (folklore). For every eps>0 there is an explicit A with A+A=N_0 and sigma_A(n) <= n^eps for large n. Proof: Erdős's argument at one finite scale: put x in S subset [0,b) independently with prob p_x=min{1, K sqrt(log b/(x+1))}. For each m<2b, r_S(m) dominates sum_{x<m/2} 1_S(x)1_S(m-x), a sum of independent Bernoullis (disjoint pairs) with mean ~ K^2 log b (for m<b; O(K^2 log b) for b<=m<2b), so Pr[r_S(m)=0] <= b^{-3} and by Chernoff Pr[r_S(m) >= C K^2 log b] <= b^{-3}; union bound gives S_b with S_b+S_b containing [0,b) and R(S_b) <= C' log b. Fix b with log(2C' log b)/log b < eps, hard-code S_b, use the Lemma with constant base b: d(n) <= log_b n + 1, so sigma_A(n) <= (2R)^{log_b n + 1} = 2R n^{log(2R)/log b} <= n^eps. Fixed base can never give n^{o(1)}.

3. Theorem B (equivalence). (1) Q1 is positive iff there is a uniformly explicit family S_ell subset [0,2^ell), S_ell+S_ell containing [0,2^ell), with R(S_ell) <= ell^C. (2) Q2 is positive iff such a family exists with R(S_ell) <= exp(ell^{1-delta}) for some delta>0.
Proof. (=>) S_ell = A cap [0,2^ell): if m<2^ell and m=a+a', then a,a'<2^ell, so S_ell+S_ell covers [0,2^ell) and r_{S_ell}(m) <= sigma_A(m) <= max_{m<2^ell} sigma_A(m), which is ell^C resp. exp(ell^{1-delta}) up to constants; explicitness inherited.
(<=, part 1) Take ell_i = 2^{2^i}. For d=d(n)>=2, n >= B_d >= 2^{ell_{d-1}} so ell_{d-1} <= log n, ell_d = ell_{d-1}^2 <= (log n)^2, 2^{d-1} = log ell_{d-1} <= log log n. Hence sigma_A(n) <= 2^{d-1} prod ell_i^C = 2^{d-1} 2^{C(2^{d+1}-2)} < (log log n) ell_d^{2C} <= (log n)^{4C+1}.
(<=, part 2) Take ell_i = 2^i. Then B_d = 2^{2^d-2} <= n gives 2^d <= log n + 2, and sigma_A(n) <= 2^{d-1} exp(sum_{i<=d} 2^{i(1-delta)}) O(1) <= (log n+2) exp(C_delta (log n+2)^{1-delta}) <= exp((log n)^{1-delta/2}) for large n, C_delta=(1-2^{-(1-delta)})^{-1}. In both parts the Lemma gives A+A=N_0 and explicitness. (Squaring schedule is needed in part 1 to keep prod ell_i^C polylog; doubling in part 2 so the top digit does not overshoot log n.)
Consequently Q1/Q2 are exactly: give one poly-time predicate P(ell,x) such that S_ell={x<2^ell: P(ell,x)} is a basis of [0,2^ell) with max representation number ell^{O(1)} resp. exp(ell^{1-delta}). Random sets of density sqrt(ell/x) achieve R <= C ell, so this is a pure single-scale derandomization problem.

4. Barriers (remarks). (i) Digit constructions are multiplicative: sigma ~ prod R(S_i) with sum log b_i ~ log n, so one needs log R(S_i) <~ (log b_i)^{1-delta} for the top digits — the same problem; recursion f(b) <= 2 f(sqrt b)^2 gives f(b)=b^{Theta(1)}. Theorem B is the sharp statement that nothing is lost or gained by gluing scales. (ii) Per-digit R(S_ell)=O(1) for all ell would, by compactness, give an infinite order-2 basis with bounded representation function, contradicting the Erdős–Turán conjecture; so building blocks must have R -> infinity and the issue is the rate. (iii) Constructions whose counts are controlled by divisor/norm-form equations (e.g. r_2(m) <= 4 d(m)) are capped at max d(m) = n^{(log 2 + o(1))/log log n}, the JPSZ shape; beating it requires additive energy not governed by multiplicative structure. (iv) O(log b)-wise independence with Erdős marginals suffices for the moment-method tail bounds at each m, so small-bias/k-wise spaces of size b^{Theta(log b)} contain good points, but no poly(log b)-time way to name one is available; conditional expectations with Chernoff-type pessimistic estimators on the independent pair variables plausibly give a poly(b)-time construction, exponentially worse than required.

5. Conclusion. Q1 and Q2 remain unanswered. Proved: Theorem A (explicit sigma_A(n) <= n^eps) and Theorem B (exact equivalence of Q1/Q2 with a uniformly explicit single-scale finite basis problem with R(S_ell) <= ell^{O(1)} resp. exp(ell^{1-delta})). What remains is exactly the single-scale derandomization in Theorem B.
</solution>
